title: Children's Online Safety Security Checklist
metaDescription: Essential checklist to protect children's online privacy and safety. COPPA compliance, parental controls, and internet safety tips for kids.
intro: Protecting children online requires a multi-layered approach combining parental controls, privacy settings, and education. This checklist covers essential steps to safeguard your child's digital privacy and ensure compliance with children's privacy laws.

items.task: Install privacy-focused browser like Incognito Browser
items.why: Standard browsers often track user activity and collect data. Privacy browsers block trackers and provide better protection for children.
items.howTo: Download Incognito Browser or similar privacy-focused browser. Enable safe browsing mode and disable data collection features. Set as default browser for child's device.

items.task: Enable comprehensive parental controls on all devices
items.why: Parental controls filter inappropriate content, limit screen time, and restrict access to certain websites and apps.
items.howTo: Use built-in parental controls (Screen Time on iOS, Family Link on Android) or third-party solutions like Qustodio. Set age-appropriate content filters and time limits.

items.task: Enable SafeSearch on all search engines
items.why: SafeSearch filters explicit content from search results, reducing exposure to inappropriate material.
items.howTo: Go to Google, Bing, and other search engines. Enable SafeSearch in settings. Lock the setting with parental controls to prevent changes.

items.task: Disable location services for unnecessary apps
items.why: Location data can be used to track children's movements and create detailed profiles of their activities.
items.howTo: Review location permissions in device settings. Disable location access for apps that don't need it. Keep enabled only for essential safety apps.

items.task: Set all social media accounts to private
items.why: Private profiles prevent strangers from viewing your child's posts, photos, and personal information.
items.howTo: Go to privacy settings on each platform (Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat). Enable private account mode. Review follower requests together with your child.

items.task: Restrict who can contact your child online
items.why: Limiting contact to known friends reduces risk of cyberbullying, predators, and unwanted interactions.
items.howTo: In messaging apps and social platforms, set contacts to 'friends only.' Disable message requests from strangers. Review friend/follower lists regularly.

items.task: Disable data sharing with third parties
items.why: Children's data is valuable to marketers and should be protected under COPPA regulations.
items.howTo: Review privacy settings on all apps and services. Opt out of data sharing, targeted advertising, and analytics. Choose minimal data collection options.

items.task: Verify COPPA compliance for services used by children under 13
items.why: COPPA requires parental consent for data collection from children under 13 and limits what information can be gathered.
items.howTo: Check privacy policies of websites and apps. Look for COPPA compliance statements. Use kid-safe versions of services when available (YouTube Kids, Messenger Kids).

items.task: Teach children about online privacy basics
items.why: Educated children make better decisions about sharing personal information and recognizing online risks.
items.howTo: Explain what personal information is (name, address, school). Discuss why strangers shouldn't have this info. Practice scenarios about what to share and what to keep private.

items.task: Establish clear reporting procedures for uncomfortable situations
items.why: Children need to know they can safely report concerning interactions without fear of losing internet privileges.
items.howTo: Create an open communication policy. Teach children to report cyberbullying, inappropriate messages, or uncomfortable requests immediately without punishment.

items.task: Create strong, unique passwords for all accounts
items.why: Weak passwords can lead to account takeovers, exposing personal information and allowing impersonation.
items.howTo: Use a password manager to generate strong passwords. Enable two-factor authentication where available. Regularly update passwords for important accounts.

items.task: Regularly review your child's digital footprint
items.why: Information shared online can persist forever and affect future opportunities including college admissions and employment.
items.howTo: Search your child's name online monthly. Review social media posts together. Delete inappropriate content and adjust privacy settings as needed.
